Key Responsibilities

1. Requirement Gathering & Documentation

• Partner with HR leadership and business stakeholders to understand reporting and analytics requirements

• Translate business needs into clear Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) and functional specifications

• Prioritize and scope requests based on business impact, urgency, and feasibility

2. Data Structuring & Cleaning

• Consolidate HR data from multiple sources, including HRMS, payroll, attendance, recruitment, and exit data

• Clean, validate, and structure raw datasets into reliable, analysis-ready formats

• Build and maintain standardized templates and master datasets to ensure consistency and minimize reporting errors

3. Dashboard & Visualization Development

• Design and build interactive, intuitive dashboards (Power BI, Tableau, or advanced Excel/Google Sheets) covering key HR metrics such as attrition, headcount, hiring funnel, engagement, and performance

• Ensure dashboards are accurate, regularly refreshed, and easy to interpret for non-technical audiences

• Continuously refine visualizations based on stakeholder feedback and evolving business priorities

4. Advanced Excel & Spreadsheet Management

• Build and maintain complex formulas, pivot tables, and data models in Excel/Google Sheets

• Maintain organized, error-free trackers for headcount, compensation, attendance, and other core HR datasets

5. AI & Emerging Tools Capability

• Leverage AI tools (e.g., Chat GPT, Claude, Copilot) to accelerate analysis, summarize large datasets, and generate quick insights

• Stay current on AI-assisted analytics tools and recommend adoption where it improves efficiency

• Explore opportunities to apply predictive analytics to HR use cases such as attrition risk and hiring forecasts

6. Insights & Reporting

• Convert data into clear, actionable insights that support leadership decision-making

• Prepare periodic (weekly, monthly, quarterly) HR MIS reports with a high standard of accuracy

• Proactively identify trends, anomalies, and improvement opportunities within HR data, rather than relying solely on ad-hoc requests

Required Skills & Qualifications

Technical Skills

• Advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets (pivot tables, lookups, array formulas)

• Strong working knowledge of at least one visualization tool: Power BI, Tableau, or Looker Studio

• Basic to intermediate SQL knowledge is an advantage

• Comfortable adopting AI tools to enhance analytical productivity

Functional Skills

• Solid understanding of core HR processes and metrics (attrition, recruitment funnel, headcount planning, performance, engagement)

• Demonstrated experience writing BRDs and converting business requirements into technical deliverables

• Strong data cleaning and structuring skills across multiple, often unstructured, data sources

Soft Skills

• Excellent stakeholder management — able to extract clear requirements from non-technical HR and business users

• High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data accuracy

• Ability to simplify complex datasets into clear, compelling visual narratives

• Self-driven and proactive in identifying reporting gaps and improvement opportunities

Education

• Graduate/Postgraduate in any discipline; background in Statistics, Commerce, HR, or Data Analytics preferred

• Certifications in Power BI, Tableau, or Data Analytics are an added advantage

Experience Requirement

3–5 years of relevant experience in HR analytics, MIS, or data analytics roles. Strong preference for HR domain exposure; candidates with a robust analytics background and willingness to learn HR processes will also be considered.

Why This Role Matters

This is a high-impact, hybrid role for someone who can own the complete cycle — understanding the business problem, structuring the underlying data, building the visualization, and delivering the final insight. This person will serve as the analytical backbone of the HR function, directly enabling faster and more informed people decisions.

Location: Chandigarh
Employment Type: Full-time

Role Overview:

The Associate – Student Welfare Services will play a pivotal role in fostering a supportive, inclusive, and engaging environment for students. This individual will be responsible for implementing welfare initiatives, managing student grievances, supporting mental health and well-being programs, and facilitating access to essential student resources and services. The role demands empathy, strong interpersonal skills, and a proactive attitude toward enhancing the overall student experience.

Key RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Student Support Services:

    • Serve as the first point of contact for student welfare inquiries.

    • Facilitate access to mental health and counseling resources.

    • Provide guidance on academic and non-academic support systems.

  • Welfare Program Implementation:

    • Assist in designing and executing programs aimed at enhancing student well-being, including orientation, wellness workshops, awareness campaigns, and peer support initiatives.

    • Coordinate with internal departments and external agencies to deliver these programs effectively.

  • Grievance Management:

    • Receive, document, and escalate student complaints and concerns to relevant departments.

    • Track resolution progress and ensure timely and appropriate responses.

  • Communication & Outreach:

    • Develop and disseminate student welfare materials such as newsletters, policy briefs, and event promotions.

    • Manage communication channels including email, social media, and welfare portals.

  • Event Planning and Coordination:

    • Organize student welfare events, awareness days, and training sessions.

    • Collaborate with student bodies and clubs for inclusive engagement.

  • Data Management & Reporting:

    • Maintain records of student cases, participation in welfare activities, and feedback.

    • Assist in preparing periodic reports and presentations on welfare metrics and outcomes.

Key Requirements:

  • EDUCATION: Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Education, or related field. A Master’s degree is preferred.

  • Experience: 1-3 years of relevant experience in student affairs, counseling, or administrative support in an educational environment.

  • Skills:

    • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.

    • High emotional intelligence and cultural sensitivity.

    • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information.

    • Organizational and problem-solving capabilities.

    • Proficiency in MS Office; experience with student information systems is a plus.

Preferred Attributes:

  • Experience working with young adults in educational settings.

  • Awareness of mental health issues and student welfare trends.

  • Ability to handle multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

  • Passionate about student development and engagement.
